Actually block computes dy*(x*r).to(fp16) then tl.sum over rows axis — product still FP16. Hmm, error 8.12 at M=512, N=200. Could be the h computed differently in block path: x*r[:,None]... same. Actually why does block dw differ? tl.sum(dy * (...), 0) — dy*fp16 gives fp16; sum in fp16? tl.sum of an fp16 tensor may accumulate in fp16! That would cause rounding error. dx_path diff is only 1 ulp. So block kernel likely sums the dw terms in FP16 (or the product term promoted), producing error ratio 8.12. This supports c3 partially — but c3 claim is about path disagreement / boundary. Evidence: dw differs by 0.0738 between paths, block dw ratio 8.12 > 1. So c3 confirmed.
